mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the central bank maintains accommodative policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness that depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for three consecutive months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative earnings expectations and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of instances (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) creates policy constraint uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth above 2.0% (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 45% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 95.0 (INDPRO) for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profitability, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO remains below 95.0 for two consecutive months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) combined with declining employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.1%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 700.0 thousand units for two consecutive months indicate weakening housing market conditions that reduce consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST remains below 700.0 for two consecutive months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
